questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exciting courses and living in a country with high safety

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved meeting new people and having new kind of courses. But due to the Netherland's housing crisis, was it extremely difficult to find accomdation. At one point, I considered withdrawing because I had no home. The time looking for accomdation was so stressfull. Because of this housing crisis, a lot of the other students also lived pretty far away. If I could go back, I (sadly) would have chosen another country because of this.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy - they have a help desk, where you can ask questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had an help desk, where they made you your student card etc. You could also just ask their information desk, if you had questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. They offer housing accomdation, but they have very few rooms. You have to be very fast and pay a fee, but I would definetely sign up for that. I hestitated at first, because I found the fee pretty expensive, but when I changed my mind, everything was taken (also before their deadline), so you have to be quick.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Ask everyone in your network if they know some one who lives in the Netherlands. There are also some student housing, where the room mates require you to speak Dutch, so it is even harder to find something as an international student. Also - you can look at web pages where other Danish students go to the Netherlands and see if they post anything about avaliable rooms. But yes, it is difficult.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They need more rooms. There where so many internationals who struggled with accomdation, and with this housing crisis, does it seem pretty sad, that the internationals has to worry so much about finding a place to live.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just remember getting to the help desk and get my student card etc. It was all very chill

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They also had an information desk, where you could ask questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They were helpful - I found the process easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wished they had more courses to choose from as a master student

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I felt like the way the courses was taught was very different. One of my courses was pretty difficult, but it was also the one course where I felt like I learned the most.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Some of it was pretty similiar. It was very discussion based, which I liked.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Gender / genre: New Approaches to the Human in Critical and Cultural Theory
Interculturality: Key Concepts
Popular Music: Pleasure, Ideology, Technology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Gender/genre and Popular music

If you want to challenge yourself (and your English skills) I will choose Gender/genre, but I did find the course to be pretty difficult.
The Popular Music course was very nice and remined me a lot of some films courses that I have had before at home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation is very expensive. If you live nearby, I would recommend to buy or rent a bike. But if you commute, its pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were the Erasmus events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to the different Erasmus Events and find all the what app chats. It was very easy to meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit some of the other cities as well. Not only Amsterdam, but also Utrecht. Leiden is also a very cosy city to walk around in.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: All the internationals are very open, so talk to some of them in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, it's very similiar do Danish culture

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They speak very well English. And they wave and say goodbye when they leave the bus, that was pretty cute

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find accomdation first. It's very nice to live with other people, so see if you can figure out if other people are looking for a place as well.
2. They have computers in the library that everyone can use - sometimes you have to "book" them
3. Join all the different social stuff you can in the beginning, so you can get to meet people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They have a weird grading system. It is apparently almost impossible to get their highest score (10),
 so you should not feel bad if your grade seems lover than what you anticipated. 
But besides the grade, do you also get feedback from your exams, which I really liked.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people! I have met some very nice people that I plan to visit.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accomdation. It really did affect my experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
